To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Indexed Lookup Eger algorithm is the most efficient algorithm for keyword search for smallest LCAs and that it is the most efficient of all known LCA algorithms when the keyword frequency is skewed.

(1) we propose efficient keyword search algorithms for XML documents, (2) we show that the Indexed Lookup Eger algorithm outperforms all existing keyword search algorithms by orders of magnitudes for queries containing keywords of significantly different frequencies, and (3) we propose an algorithm to answer Lowest Comman Ancestor queries for XML documents.

(1) the Indexed Lookup Eger algorithm is orders of magnitude faster than the Stack algorithm, (2) the Scan Eager algorithm outperforms Indexed Lookup Eager for queries with keywords of similar frequencies, (3) the Stack algorithm is more efficient than Scan Eager when the query contains a large number of keywords, (4) the LCA algorithm outperforms the Stack algorithm for LCA queries with a small number of keywords.
In summary, our research is concerned with

efficient keyword search for XML data and the corresponding LCA queries, and we believe that our results are useful for XML data management in general and for the development of new XML search engines.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Indexed Lookup Eger algorithm is the best choice for the general case, and the Scan Eager is a good choice when the keywords have similar frequency.
the Eager algorithm is the best choice for keyword search on XML databases.
the proposed algorithms are the most efficient ones for the smallest LCA problem, as well as for the keyword search problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed and implemented efficient algorithms to answer keyword queries, which return the smallest set of XML documents containing all keywords, and to answer LCA queries in XML databases.
the Eager algorithm is a good choice when the keywords are of significantly different frequencies and Stack is a good choice otherwise.
we have proposed and evaluated efficient algorithms for the problem of finding smallest trees containing a given set of keywords in XML documents.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Indexed Lookup Eger algorithm, which is simple and easy to implement, is orders of magnitude more efficient than the Stack algorithm for keyword queries with significantly different frequencies, and is competitive with the Stack algorithm in the case of queries with similar frequencies.
efficient keyword search in XML databases is possible and can be achieved with a combination of novel algorithms, indexing techniques and query processing optimizations.
the Eager algorithms are orders of magnitude more efficient than the Stack algorithm when the query contains a keyword that appears in a small number of trees.
